title: Double Trouble
summary: Interrupt two rook lines at once: one guards promotion and the other guards the king.

nodes.question: How can White combine promotion with a king attack?
nodes.explanation: The rook on d2 stops d8=Q. Kf4 can restrict Kh4 while Be4 supports a mating net.

nodes.question: Which defensive line can Black keep open?
nodes.explanation: Bd3 interrupts the d-file and the third rank simultaneously. Either rook capture releases another White threat.

branches.title: Capture with the c-rook: promotion releases the attack
commentary: Begin after ...Rd2 in the seven-piece phase. Earlier ...g2+ and Kxg2 belong to source context.
Kf4 controls g3, g4 and g5. White prepares an h-file attack against Kh4.
Rc3 guards the third rank, preparing to meet an h-file check by interposing a rook.
Bd3 sacrifices the bishop on the intersection of both defensive lines. It blocks Rd2’s promotion defense and Rc3’s horizontal defense.
Rcxd3 accepts with the c-rook, leaving c3 and moving that rook onto the d-file.
d8=Q+ promotes with check along d8–e7–f6–g5–h4. White uses the cleared third rank in the coming attack.
Rxd8 removes the queen with the rook from d3. The promotion has diverted that rook away from the king’s defensive rank.
Rh1+ checks along the h-file. It wins, but is not yet mate: the remaining rook can block on h2.
Rh2 is the sole legal interposition, independently supplied to complete the source’s mating claim accurately.
Rxh2# gives actual mate. Kf4 covers the g-file flights and Rh2 controls the h-file; the distant rook cannot stop this check.

branches.explanation: Rxh2# gives actual mate. Kf4 covers the g-file flights and Rh2 controls the h-file; the distant rook cannot stop this check.

branches.title: Capture with the d-rook: clear the promotion file
commentary: Compare capturing the interference bishop with the rook that guarded promotion.
Rdxd3 vacates d2. Black keeps its c-rook on c3 but loses direct control of d8.
Rh1+ checks along the h-file and forces a defensive response before promotion.
Rh3 is the source’s illustrated rook block, moving the rook from d3 to h3. It prevents immediate mate but leaves the d-file open.
d8=Q+ promotes with check along the diagonal toward Kh4. The rook on h3 still blocks White’s h-file rook, but the new queen supplies a different attack.
Kh5 is the only legal king response. Kf4 covers the g-file escape squares and h3 is occupied by Black’s rook.
Qg5# is the source’s actual mating finish. Kf4 protects Qg5, the queen covers g6 and h6, and Black cannot interpose against the adjacent queen check.
branches.explanation: Qg5# is the source’s actual mating finish. Kf4 protects Qg5, the queen covers g6 and h6, and Black cannot interpose against the adjacent queen check.

branches.title: Try to escape with the king
commentary: Compare the source’s king escape instead of the rook’s ...Rc3 defense.
Kf4 restricts the black king and prepares the rook attack.
Kh5 tries to run upward, but Be4 controls g6 and h7 while the white king controls g5.
Rh1+ checks on the open h-file. A rook block is still possible, so this is not immediate mate.
Rh2 is an independently supplied forced interposition from d2.
Rxh2# is actual mate. The bishop covers g6 and the king covers g4 and g5, closing the remaining flights.

branches.explanation: Rxh2# is actual mate. The bishop covers g6 and the king covers g4 and g5, closing the remaining flights.

exercises.prompt: Why does one bishop sacrifice affect two defenses?
exercises.answer: d3 lies on the d-file rook’s path to d8 and the c3 rook’s path toward the h-file. Capturing with either rook releases the other threat.

exercises.prompt: Why distinguish a winning check from checkmate?
exercises.answer: A defender can still interpose a rook on h2 in the illustrated h-file attacks. Capturing that blocker gives actual mate; the winning plan remains sound.

startContext: Begin after ...Rd2 at 40 seconds, with seven pieces. The earlier eight-piece opening and pawn lure remain context. The double interference and both rook captures are checked. Forced ...Rh2 Rxh2# completions are independently supplied where the source calls the earlier check mate.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.

sourceCorrections.claim: After the c-rook capture and queen sacrifice, Rh1 is called checkmate.
sourceCorrections.correction: Rh1+ still allows the sole ...Rh2 interposition, then Rxh2# gives actual mate. These independently supplied final plies preserve the source winning idea. The same block-and-capture finish is checked independently in the king-escape comparison.
